name: Lactase enzyme
short: Allergy: one man had systemic reactions to a lactase supplement; one earlier anaphylaxis; workers sensitised. Infants with colic: adverse events as placebo (162 infants), none in 3 trials.
text: Infants with colic (drops added to breast milk or formula): in a placebo-controlled trial in 162 infants under 5 months, adverse events were a stated secondary outcome and the adverse-event profile was comparable between lactase and placebo; a Cochrane review of dietary changes for colic states that there were no adverse effects in any of the three lactase trials (138 infants) it assessed. Preterm infants (a different population): in a trial in 60 preterm infants with lactose intolerance, no adverse reactions associated with the lactase additive were observed, and a Cochrane review of the one trial of lactase-treated feeds in 130 preterm infants found no adverse effects. Allergy (adults; case reports and a workplace survey): a 48-year-old man with eczema, asthma and rhinoconjunctivitis had four systemic reactions, with mucosal swelling and asthma symptoms, after ice cream, each time just after taking a lactase enzyme supplement, and had a strongly positive skin test to it; the authors note one earlier reported case of anaphylaxis without describing it. A 2016 case report, which calls itself the first documented anaphylactic reaction to supplemental lactase, describes a 38-year-old woman who had swelling around both eyes, shortness of breath and throat tightening after swallowing a lactase tablet, and a strongly positive skin test to the tablet (the man's report does not say whether this is the case it notes). In a lactase tablet factory, 9 of 13 workers were sensitised to lactase, which can cause allergic asthma and rhinitis when breathed in. Possible interaction: in a retrospective study of infants aged 0 to 6 months with lactose intolerance (not a colic trial), the response to oral lactase was lower in infants also given simethicone for colic symptoms, and the authors suggest a possible interaction that might reduce the effect of lactase. The infant abstracts report no data on allergic reactions in infants.
